summary: Prove an unattended multi-task night run with real workers
description: Validate the completed serial chain against a representative disposable project using real supported workers and authorized release targets. Hearthhold is a source of representative cases, not permission to modify its product or saves. Scope and mandate: .go/plans/autonomy-first.json. Reuse released ABC/advice/readiness behavior; implement only this delta.
acceptance: Before model calls, freeze a concrete pilot repository, allowed work, worker profiles, shared budget and publication/deployment targets from actual authority; missing choices remain explicit blockers, never invented consent.

A real unattended run starts with sufficiently concrete user intent, explores and materializes work, completes multiple separately delivered tasks, repairs a genuine or controlled fault and survives one documented interruption without manual per-task dispatch.

Record actual elapsed unattended time, task progress, user interventions, repair/release results and observed usage. No eight-hour or zero-intervention claim unless measured; stop early if the goal is fulfilled rather than inventing work.

Read back remote/live versions, preserve original outcomes/vision/architecture links, prove Git state and produce the morning report. Failed attempts remain evidence. A fixture double or hand-steered sequence does not satisfy this live proof.
Update the public autonomy capability assessment only to the level demonstrated; publish no private pilot data or local saves.

Complete this independently shippable stack change with content-bound checks/critic, scoped commit/push, immutable release and remote readback; preserve user dirt and historical evidence. Current request authorizes planning only; no execution or publication starts during intake.
